title: Quarterly anchoring workshop — sprint anchors and contingency lanes for hosted model lineup
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Objective: Run a cross-functional anchoring workshop that translates quarterly OKRs into concrete sprint anchors, guardrail budgets (latency/cost), and contingency/fallback lanes for the hosted API model catalog. Scope: hosted endpoints (tiered), model rotation windows, canary timing, capacity hedges (Dedicated fallback), and runbook triggers. Out of scope: private deployments & on-prem rollout specifics. Goals: 1) Produce a prioritized list of 6 sprint anchors with owners and acceptance criteria; 2) Define two fallback lanes per anchor (region, model-variant, or degraded-quality fallback) and their automatic routing policies; 3) Create guardrail budgets mapping OKR targets to latency/cost budgets and signal thresholds that trigger rollback/canary extension; 4) Publish a one-page exec summary + handoff deck for engineering and SRE. Acceptance criteria: - Sprint anchors have clear owners, estimates, and dependency lists. - Fallback lanes are codified as policy examples (routing rules + thresholds). - Guardrail budgets include concrete thresholds, telemetry panels, and alert rules. - Handoff artifacts (Confluence + PR template + GitHub issue skeletons) available. Success metrics: - Reduction in triage time for model rollback to < 30 minutes during staged canaries. - Defined guardrail alerts for top 3 endpoints covering 80% of hosted traffic. - 90% of sprint anchors scoped with engineering estimate and capacity hedge. Risks and trade-offs: prioritizing short-term rollbacks vs long-lived canaries may increase false positives; aggressive batching/quantization recommendations may impact latency SLAs. Next steps: finish workshop synthesis doc, schedule follow-up with SRE for alert tuning, create sub-issues for each sprint anchor.
acceptance_criteria: 6 sprint anchors with owners and estimates
Guardrail budgets mapped to dashboards and alerts
